title: routing: circuit breaker state machine w/ hysteresis + persistent state
author: Ravi Menon
release_notes: Internal: adds routing-side circuit breaker state machine with hysteresis + persistence. No customer-facing changes yet (feature-flagged).
description:
Context: part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (ENG-4821). Routing needs a deterministic breaker state model that (a) avoids flapping, (b) survives process restarts/rollouts, and (c) exposes enough telemetry for SRE/oncall to reason about why we’re shedding.

This PR implements the core breaker state machine in the routing service. It introduces a per-key breaker (keyed by model+region+tier) with CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN states, configurable thresholds, hysteresis windows, cooldowns, and persistence. This is intentionally the routing primitive only; integrating capacity signals as inputs is a follow-up step (ENG-4825), and edge/runtime shedding will consume the breaker decision via the existing routing decision path.

Key behaviors (aligned to ADR-0148):
- CLOSED → OPEN when failure/overload signals exceed open_threshold for open_window and min_samples.
- OPEN → HALF_OPEN after cooldown_ms; HALF_OPEN allows a capped probe rate (probe_concurrency + probe_rps) to test recovery.
- HALF_OPEN → CLOSED when success criteria are met for close_window (again with min_samples).
- HALF_OPEN → OPEN if failures exceed half_open_open_threshold within half_open_window.
- Hysteresis: separate open vs close thresholds + windows; optional exponential backoff on repeated OPEN transitions.
- Reason tracking: state transitions record the primary signal + top contributors for debugging and oncall snapshots.

Persistence:
- Adds a small persistence layer backed by Redis (routing-controlplane Redis cluster) with TTL.
- State is written on transitions (and periodically via a low-rate sync) to survive pod restarts.
- Uses a schema version field to allow migration.

API surface:
- Adds internal gRPC endpoints for querying breaker state and forcing overrides (intended for admin-only tooling; requested by INT-1182). Override path is guarded behind RBAC + config flag; only supports scoped overrides with max duration.
- Adds evaluation entrypoint used by routing decisions: EvaluateBreaker(key, signals) → (decision, state_snapshot).

Telemetry:
- Metrics: breaker_state{state,key_hash,region,tier}, breaker_transition_total{from,to,reason}, breaker_open_seconds, breaker_eval_total{decision}, breaker_override_total.
- Tracing: adds breaker.state and breaker.reason as span attributes; avoids high-cardinality labels by hashing model ids and limiting tier/region dimensions.

Rollout:
- Feature-flagged behind routing.breakers.enabled (default false).
- When disabled, routing behavior remains unchanged and no Redis writes occur.

Testing:
- Adds deterministic unit tests for state transitions, cooldown, and probe behavior.
- Adds integration test with Redis container in CI to validate persistence + TTL.

Notes:
- This PR deliberately does not choose final thresholds. Defaults are conservative placeholders; SRE will tune per region/model class in ENG-4828.
- Open questions for follow-up: key cardinality and long-tail model ids; we may need explicit allowlists for breaker enabling per model family during canary.

References: ADR-0148 (breaker state model + hysteresis).

review_conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): The overall structure looks good. Two questions: (1) do we risk breaker flapping if signals are bursty and our window is too short? (2) can we make sure we don’t write to Redis on every eval?

Ravi Menon (author): (1) Agree. This PR includes separate open/close thresholds + cooldown_ms and min_samples gating. I also added optional transition_backoff_ms that increases on repeated OPEN transitions. Threshold tuning still TBD. (2) Redis writes are only on state transitions plus a low-rate sync (every 30s) for long-running processes; eval path is in-memory.

Christine Wong (review): Can we align naming with ADR-0148 and include explicit half-open behavior in tests? Also, please add a metric that lets oncall answer “how long have we been open?”

Ravi Menon (author): Updated names to match ADR terms (open_window, close_window, half_open_window). Added tests for HALF_OPEN probe limiter + reopen behavior. Added breaker_open_seconds as a gauge derived from open_since.

Peter Holtz (review): Concern about cardinality: breaker_state with model id is a trap. Please don’t label with raw model.

Ravi Menon (author): Good catch. Replaced raw model_id label with key_hash and included region/tier only. Added a debug-only log line (sampled) that includes the raw key for incident triage.

Jordan Lee (review): Override endpoint: please ensure it cannot be used to create infinite open state. Also make sure override duration is bounded.

Ravi Menon (author): Override requires RBAC role routing-admin and is gated behind routing.breakers.allow_overrides flag. Added max_override_duration_ms (defaults 15m) and disallow “permanent” overrides. Overrides expire automatically.

Allison Grant (review): Tracing attributes look fine; please make sure the reason enum is stable and not free-form.

Ravi Menon (author): Implemented BreakerReason as a fixed enum (OVERLOAD_QUEUE, GPU_SATURATION, LATENCY_SPIKE, ERROR_RATE, MANUAL_OVERRIDE, UNKNOWN). No arbitrary strings.

Mina Haddad (final): Approved. Please add a short section to README describing feature flag and how to query state for debugging.

Ravi Menon (author): Added README section with example internal RPC and feature flag notes.

Result: Approved by Mina Haddad, Christine Wong, Peter Holtz, Jordan Lee, Allison Grant.
post_merge_notes: Follow-ups: (1) wire capacity signals into EvaluateBreaker inputs (ENG-4825), (2) add runbook guidance for overrides + audit logging for override usage, (3) canary-enable for 1-2 models in us-east behind per-key allowlist once thresholds land (ENG-4828/ENG-4834).
